title: Call for 2027 Participation
content: Call for Submissions Heyscotty 2026-07-29T17:45:40+00:00 Call for Conference Participation Position yourself at the forefront of scientific innovation by contributing to Pittcon 2027. Whether you are an established researcher or an emerging voice, this is an opportunity to share your work with a global audience of peers and industry leaders and to help shape a dynamic and forward-looking technical program. Learn More Call for 2027 Submissions Pittcon offers a range of high-visibility presentation formats, including Invited Symposia, Organized Sessions, Oral Sessions, and Poster Presentations, each designed to highlight impactful research and foster meaningful connections. Oral Sessions Present your research in a 20-minute talk focused on the scientific questions most important to your work. Sessions are organized by topic, methodology, or application, bringing together up to seven speakers to share advances and insights. This platform strengthens your professional profile while creating opportunities for collaboration and connections with laboratories and organizations worldwide. Opens 6-1-2026 (closes 9-28-2026) Submit Now Poster Sessions Showcase your research on the exposition floor and engage directly with attendees and exhibitors during a dedicated two-hour presentation window. This interactive format allows for in-depth discussions with those most interested in your work, fostering meaningful connections, potential collaborations, and opportunities to connect with future employers and research partners. Opens 7-13-2026 (closes 10-15-2026 undergrad 11-20-2026) Submit Now Networking Roundtables Propose and lead an interactive networking session where participants engage in open, peer-driven discussions around shared challenges and ideas. Included with full registration, these informal sessions emphasize collaboration, knowledge exchange, and meaningful dialogue without the structure of traditional presentations. To encourage discussions, Networking Roundtable rooms are equipped only with a flip chart, and no A/V equipment. Opens 7-13-2026 (closes 9-21-2026) Submit Now Workshops Propose a hands-on session designed to deliver practical, interactive learning experiences. In this 90-minute format, facilitators guide participants through engaging activities that encourage participation, discussion, and collaborative problem-solving. Leading a workshop offers a meaningful opportunity to support skill development, share expertise, and connect with attendees in a dynamic, learning-focused environment. Rooms are equipped with a presentation projector. Please note that workshop sessions are for non-commercial scientific activities; any promotional or solicitation activities, such as; scanning participants badges or distributing corporate collateral, is strictly prohibited. Opens 7-13-2026 (closes 9-21-2026) Submit Now Invited Symposia As an organizer, you have the opportunity to curate a high-profile session by bringing together leading experts in your field. Each invited speaker is allotted a 30-minute presentation to highlight impactful research and insights. These distinguished sessions offer speakers complimentary registration, and eligibility for travel support and hotel accommodations, reflecting the prestige and recognition associated with participation in an invited symposium. Submissions are closed Opens 4-13-2026 (closes 7-10-2026) Organized Sessions As an organizer, you can develop a focused session centered on a specific area of research, bringing together up to seven speakers to explore a common theme. Each speaker is allotted 20 minutes to share how their work contributes to broader scientific advancements and ongoing conversations in the field. Complimentary registration is provided to all speakers in recognition of their valuable contributions. Submissions are closed Opens 4-13-2026 (closes 7-10-2026) Short Courses Short Courses are professional-quality classes held during conference week each year. We are now accepting short course proposals in all areas of analytical chemistry and applied spectroscopy in a variety of scientific disciplines. Areas of special focus include Instrumentation, Statistics and Data Processing, Artificial Intelligence, Chemical and Elemental Analysis, Method Development, Analysis of Biologics and Biopharmaceuticals, Environmental Analyses, Food Science, Laboratory Safety, Professional Development, and Leadership. Submissions are closed Opens 5-1-2026 (closes 6-15-2026) Session descriptions that more strongly make the case in these three areas will have the best chance for a high-profile spot in the Technical Program. Cutting-Edge Research and Innovations: Our priority is to feature research and innovations that are not only groundbreaking but also highly pertinent to current analytical methods and techniques.
